idiom_name: layout template + named fragment regions + fragment resolver
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: split the page into a layout that declares named regions and a set of fragments that each render one region (or one repeated item) from explicit inputs. The page composer decides which fragment fills which region - by configuration, request state or role - and the engine's include primitive resolves the reference and renders it in place, either in the calling context or with an explicitly passed parameter scope. Keep fragments free of ambient state, escape at the fragment boundary, and cache parsed templates; where the language offers typed template functions or components (Twirl, Askama, Razor, TSX), prefer them because renames and missing inputs become build errors instead of render-time surprises.
code_sketch:
page(model):
    out = layout_begin(title=model.title)        # regions: header, content, footer
    out += resolve("header")                      # one atomic subview
    for item in model.items:
        out += resolve("row", item)               # repeated subview
    out += resolve("footer")
    return out
pitfalls: Fragments that read ambient context instead of declared parameters cannot be reused and fail silently when included from another page.
Building fragment names or paths from request data turns dynamic inclusion into template injection or local-file disclosure.
Composing every fragment at request time without caching parsed templates (or whole pages) multiplies render cost per region.
